Checked the correctness lens's main claim that notify() is not called at gates.js:63. It is false: the worktree's substrate/gates.js imports notify at line 16 and runs `rec.delivery = await notify(rec)` at line 63, exactly as in the diff.

Traced why the tests saw rec.delivery as undefined. The tests in .artifacts/tests/t1-gate-delivery/ import '../../../substrate/test/helpers.js', which resolves to /home/user/company-graph/substrate/test/helpers.js. Its cli() spawns path.join(REPO,'substrate','gates.js'), where REPO is the main tree. The main tree's substrate/gates.js has no notify import, so the tests ran against the base code, not the worktree. That explains both the undefined delivery and the 0 requests.

Found a second problem on the test side. cli() uses spawnSync, which blocks the parent's event loop, so the 127.0.0.1 server started inside the same test process cannot answer while the child runs. HTTP-path tests (AC-4/5/6/10/11) built this way cannot see requests even against a correct implementation. This is a defect in the test harness, not in the implementation.

r1: upheld correctness at .artifacts/tests/t1-gate-delivery|TestSet criteria_coverage property: The finding targets the TestSet submission's criteria_coverage field, not the correctness of AC-10's assertions. The fixer's own dispute confirms the underlying fact: tests_ref pointed to a single file (c5-AC-10-token-never-leaks.test.js), only 3 tests executed, and all 14 ACs were nonetheless claimed as covered. That is a genuine misrepresentation in the artifact under review — a TestSet claiming coverage it did not actually exercise is a real defect in how the Test Author's output represents the spec's acceptance criteria, independent of whether AC-10 itself is well-tested. Reclassifying this as 'packaging mismatch' rather than 'test defect' does not change that criteria_coverage was false; a false coverage claim is squarely something the correctness lens is entitled to flag. Nothing in the spec (ledger/runs/k12/spec-wi-c5-gate-delivery.json) sanctions submitting partial coverage while declaring full coverage, so this is not an out-of-scope ask or an already-blocked attack — it is a legitimate accuracy defect in the submitted TestSet.
